title: 10 Best Budae Jjigae (Army Stew) in Seoul 2026
description: The best budae jjigae restaurants in Seoul, from the original Uijeongbu birthplace to hidden Gangnam gems. Curated from Reddit reviews with Google ratings, hours & maps.

places.name: Odeng Sikdang (오뎅식당)

redditQuotes.text: Each pot of budae-jjigae here is still served with a deep, nostalgic flavor... Sixty years after the restaurant first opened.

places.verdict: The birthplace of budae jjigae. Odeng Sikdang has been serving army stew since the 1960s — the restaurant where the entire dish was invented. A 30-minute subway ride from Seoul, but an essential pilgrimage for any army stew devotee.

comparison.best for: History buffs and food pilgrims who want the original, unmodified recipe
comparison.strengths: The literal birthplace of budae jjigae · 60+ years of history · Multiple directly-managed branches
comparison.limitations: 30-min subway from central Seoul (Uijeongbu Station, Line 1) · Mixed reviews from modern visitors expecting fancy
comparison.what to order: The original budae jjigae — order the basic version first. Add ramyeon noodles (라면사리) and extra cheese. End with rice porridge in the remaining broth.
comparison.insider tip: Go on a weekday to avoid the crowds from Budaejjigae Street tourists. The restaurant is on the official Uijeongbu Budaejjigae Street with 20+ competing shops.

places.whatToOrder: The original budae jjigae — order the basic version first. Add ramyeon noodles (라면사리) and extra cheese. End with rice porridge in the remaining broth.

places.name: Daewoo Budaejjigae (대우부대찌개)

redditQuotes.text: This legendary establishment has been serving their signature army stew since 1984... the water dropwort adds an herbal note that cuts through the richness.

places.verdict: A Gangnam institution since 1984 — Daewoo's signature twist is fresh water dropwort (minari) that cuts through the richness of the broth with a clean, herbal note. The gold standard for refined army stew within Seoul proper.

comparison.best for: The best sit-down budae jjigae experience within Seoul — elevated but authentic
comparison.strengths: 4.3★ from 1,614 reviews · 40+ years of history · Unique minari (water dropwort) addition
comparison.limitations: Closed Saturdays · Lunch/dinner split hours (closes 3-5 PM)
comparison.what to order: Their signature budae jjigae with extra minari. The water dropwort adds an herbal, refreshing note that makes this version uniquely sophisticated.
comparison.insider tip: Go for lunch — it's less crowded and you avoid the dinner rush from nearby Gangnam office workers.

places.whatToOrder: Their signature budae jjigae with extra minari. The water dropwort adds an herbal, refreshing note that makes this version uniquely sophisticated.

comparison.what to order: The standard budae jjigae with extra cheese and ramyeon noodles. The generous portions here make add-ons almost unnecessary.
comparison.insider tip: Come for a late lunch (2-3 PM) to beat the crowds. Pairs perfectly with a Hongdae nightlife crawl — line your stomach first.

comparison.insider tip: This spot was featured on Reddit as "the budae jjigae was good — you can get budae jjigae all over Seoul" but Yoojung consistently stands out.

places.name: Nolboo Budae Jjigae Hapjeong (놀부부대찌개 합정)

redditQuotes.text: If you are planning to visit normal Nolboo Budae Jjigae in Myeongdong or somewhere else, I want you to detour. We couldn't feel taste difference at all.

places.verdict: Nolboo is Korea's largest budae jjigae chain, and this Hapjeong branch is one of the rare all-you-can-eat buffet locations. For about ₩10,000, you get unlimited ham, noodles, vegetables, and even ice cream. Unbeatable value.

comparison.best for: Hungry travelers who want maximum value — all-you-can-eat army stew with unlimited toppings
comparison.strengths: AYCE for ₩10,000 · Self-service station with hams, noodles, veggies, eggs · Free ice cream
comparison.limitations: Chain restaurant feel · Basement location in Mecenatpolis mall
comparison.what to order: The Nolbu (놀부) signature stew — moderately spicy with a delicate broth. Load up on extra ham from the station. Cook your own fried egg.
comparison.insider tip: Food bloggers say there's "no taste difference" between the AYCE and regular Nolboo branches — so why pay more? The regular branches charge extra for ramyeon and udon add-ons.

places.whatToOrder: The Nolbu (놀부) signature stew — moderately spicy with a delicate broth. Load up on extra ham from the station. Cook your own fried egg.

places.name: Mama Bujji (마마부찌)

redditQuotes.text: For two people, the total cost doesn't even reach $20! Pretty amazing, right? One unique feature is that they don't charge for rice, drinks, or side dishes.

places.verdict: A no-frills, homestyle army stew shop in Noryangjin — the neighborhood known for exam-cramming students. At ₩8,500 (~$6) per person with free unlimited rice, drinks, and side dishes, it's one of the best value budae jjigae in all of Seoul. Solo dining possible.

comparison.best for: Budget travelers and solo diners who want a warm, homestyle army stew without pretension
comparison.strengths: ₩8,500 per person with unlimited rice, drinks & banchan · Solo-friendly · Run by a warm ajumma
comparison.limitations: Off the tourist trail in Noryangjin · Simple interior — function over form
comparison.what to order: The signature budae jjigae with added ramyeon noodles. Help yourself to unlimited macaroni salad, kimchi, and pickled radish from the self-service station.
comparison.insider tip: "When I arrived around 7 PM, all 15 or so tables were fully occupied. Many were dining alone" — this is the rare budae jjigae spot where solo dining is not just accepted, it's the norm.
